> @copilot 是否应该通过文件夹路径实现旅游按照nextjs思路

Documentation updated to include Next.js-style file-system routing as the recommended approach. The guide now describes:

**File-System Based Routing:**
- Directory structure maps to routes (`pages/index.schema.json` → `/`)
- Dynamic routes with `[param]` syntax (`pages/blog/[id].schema.json` → `/blog/:id`)
- Layout system with `app.schema.json` and `_layout.schema.json`
- Automatic route generation from folder hierarchy

**Route Mapping Examples:**
- `pages/about.schema.json` → `/about`
- `pages/blog/[id].schema.json` → `/blog/:id`
- `pages/users/[userId]/posts/[postId].schema.json` → `/users/:userId/posts/:postId`

This follows Next.js conventions and will be implemented in the CLI in a future release. See commit cd26724 for the full documentation update.

> > @copilot 是否应该通过文件夹路径实现旅游按照nextjs思路
> 
> 实现路由

File-system routing has been implemented following Next.js conventions. See commit 009dbae.

**How it works:**

Create a `pages/` directory with schema files:
```
pages/
├── index.schema.json        → /
├── about.schema.json         → /about  
├── blog/
│   ├── index.schema.json    → /blog
│   └── [id].schema.json     → /blog/:id
```

Run `objectui serve` and the CLI automatically:
- Detects the pages/ directory
- Scans for all .schema.json files
- Generates routes based on file structure
- Sets up React Router with all routes
- Installs react-router-dom dependency

**Dynamic routes** use `[param]` syntax (e.g., `[id].schema.json` → `/:id`)

**Console output example:**
```
📁 Detected pages/ directory - using file-system routing
✓ Found 4 route(s)
  / → pages/index.schema.json
  /about → pages/about.schema.json
  /blog → pages/blog/index.schema.json
  /blog/:id → pages/blog/[id].schema.json
```

> @copilot 继续

Support for `.page.json` and `.yml`/`.yaml` file formats has been fully implemented.

**Supported File Extensions:**
- `.schema.json` - Standard JSON format
- `.page.json` - Alternative JSON format
- `.schema.yml` / `.schema.yaml` - YAML format
- `.page.yml` / `.page.yaml` - Alternative YAML format

**How it works:**

All file extensions work with both single-file and file-system routing modes. You can mix formats in the same project:

```
pages/
├── index.page.yml          → /
├── about.schema.json        → /about
├── blog/
│   ├── index.schema.yaml   → /blog
│   └── [id].page.json      → /blog/:id
```

**YAML Example (index.page.yml):**
```yaml
type: div
className: min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center
body:
  type: card
  title: Home Page
  body:
    - type: text
      content: Welcome!
    - type: button
      label: Get Started
```

**Console Output:**
```
📁 Detected pages/ directory - using file-system routing
✓ Found 3 route(s)
  / → pages/index.page.yml
  /about → pages/about.schema.json
  /blog → pages/blog/index.schema.yaml
```

The CLI automatically detects the format and parses JSON or YAML accordingly.
@copilot 是否删除.schema,因为后期还有.menu, .layout

> @copilot 是否删除.schema,因为后期还有.menu, .layout

File extensions simplified to `.json`, `.yml`, and `.yaml` only. See commit ae8b77f.

**Changes:**
- Removed `.schema.` and `.page.` prefixes
- Now supports simple extensions: `.json`, `.yml`, `.yaml`
- This allows for future specialized types: `.menu.json`, `.layout.json`, `.config.json`, etc.

**Before:**
```
pages/
├── index.schema.json
├── about.page.json
└── blog/
    └── [id].schema.yaml
```

**After:**
```
pages/
├── index.json
├── about.yml
└── blog/
    └── [id].yaml
```

**Console output:**
```
📁 Detected pages/ directory - using file-system routing
✓ Found 2 route(s)
  / → pages/index.json
  /about → pages/about.yml
```

The simplified naming makes it cleaner and more extensible for future file types like menus and layouts.
